title: Authentication methods in Microsoft Entra ID: which ways can users prove who they are?
summary: Hold: the page overstates which changes the Authentication methods policy governs and incorrectly says migration changes security-question password reset. It also overlooks documented transaction-based SMS authentication charges and treats published Microsoft-managed campaign settings as unknown.

claims.claim: Passkey group availability and settings are managed in Microsoft Entra admin center under Entra ID > Authentication methods > Policies.
claims.quote: browse to Entra ID > Authentication methods > Policies.
claims.fix: The route stops on the method list. Extend it to 'Entra ID > Authentication methods > Policies > Passkey (FIDO2) > Enable and Target > Enable'; note that group assignments use Add target and method settings use Configure. See https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-enable-authenticator-passkey and https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-authentication-passkeys-fido2. The latter page also inserts Security after Entra ID; report that navigation difference rather than silently selecting it.

claims.fix: Keep the call and add to the row note: 'Request-body property state enables or disables the method; includeTargets assigns groups and passkey profiles; passkeyProfiles configures profile settings.' These properties appear in the cited v1.0 request.

claims.where: summary; What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Authentication strengths are Conditional Access controls that determine which method combinations can access a resource.
claims.quote: An authentication strength is a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access control that specifies which combinations of authentication methods users can use to access a resource.

claims.claim: Authentication verifies identity before granting access to apps, services, devices or networks.
claims.quote: Authentication is a security process that verifies a user's identity before granting access to apps, services, devices, or networks.

claims.claim: The policy has entries for passkeys, Authenticator, SMS, voice calls, Temporary Access Pass, certificate-based authentication and software and hardware OATH tokens.

claims.fix: Change 'hardware OATH tokens' to 'hardware OATH tokens (preview)' in this list, as marked in https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-methods.

claims.claim: Every passkey, Authenticator or Windows Hello change lands in the Authentication methods policy, where registration availability is decided.
claims.quote:
You can configure Windows Hello for Business by using the following options:
Configuration Service Provider (CSP)
Group policy (GPO)
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: 'The Authentication methods policy governs passkey and Authenticator availability; authentication strengths can restrict which methods access a resource. Windows Hello for Business enrollment is configured separately through CSP or Group Policy.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/identity-protection/hello-for-business/configure. Do not imply this policy manages every Windows Hello change.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: any policy enables it
claims.claim: Before migration is complete, enabling a method in any respected legacy or modern policy can allow registration and use despite disabling it in another.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra ID respects the settings in all of the policies so a user who is enabled for an authentication method in any policy can register and use that method. To prevent users from using a method, it must be disabled in all policies.

claims.claim: Since 30 September 2025 authentication methods can no longer be managed in the legacy policies.
claims.quote: No changes can be made to the legacy policies if Migration Complete is set, except for security questions in the SSPR policy.
claims.fix: Replace with: 'Microsoft deprecated management of authentication methods in the legacy MFA and SSPR policies from 30 September 2025, but security questions remain manageable in legacy SSPR, including after Migration Complete.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-authentication-methods-manage alongside the overview.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Security questions; What to check

The mechanism overview supports the present location but does not mention the retirement documented on the method's own page.
